h1: SEO and GEO for Houston businesses
intro: We run SEO for Houston companies that need to be found in two places: Google's results and the answers given by ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Google AI Overviews. That means technical fixes, local search across Greater Houston, content that answers buyers' real questions and a clear monthly report. Built for law firms, clinics, home services and B2B firms.

sections.h: Why Houston search is harder than it looks
p: Greater Houston is enormous. A customer in Katy and a customer in Kingwood are more than an hour apart, and Google treats them as separate local markets. A business that ranks in the Galleria can be invisible in Pearland. Personal injury, dental, roofing and HVAC are some of the most crowded local searches in the country here, and firms with large budgets have been competing for them for years.

On top of that, buyers now ask AI assistants. A plant manager asks ChatGPT for an industrial cleaning contractor near Baytown. A patient asks Gemini which clinics near the Medical Center treat a condition. If your business is not described clearly and consistently across the web, those answers name someone else. Good SEO, Houston firms are learning, now has two scoreboards.

list: Technical SEO: site speed, crawl errors, indexing, structured data and mobile performance.
Local SEO and Google Business Profile management for each location and service area.
Content: service pages, location pages and articles that answer what buyers actually ask.
Answer-first pages written so AI assistants can quote them accurately.
How your business is described across directories, review sites, industry bodies and news, so the facts match everywhere.
Outside mentions from relevant Houston and industry publications.
A monthly report in plain English: rankings, leads, AI answer checks and what we do next.

sections.h: What GEO means and why it matters here
p: Generative engine optimization, or GEO, is the work of making sure AI assistants describe your business correctly and include it when people ask for recommendations. It overlaps with SEO. Houston businesses that rank well in Google can still be missing from AI answers, so it needs its own checks. AI tools lean on clear, consistent facts: what you do, where, for whom, and what others say about you.

For a Houston company, that means your service area, specialties and credentials must be stated plainly on your own site and match what appears on directories, the Better Business Bureau, industry associations and local press. We check how ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Google AI Overviews currently describe you, fix the gaps, and recheck every month.

list: Personal injury and other law firms: practice pages for truck crashes on I-10 and I-45, refinery and plant injuries, and maritime cases, with every statute and deadline checked against Texas law.
Clinics, dental and aesthetics practices: location pages for each office, review management, and health content written with care around what can and cannot be claimed.
Home services and contractors: service-area pages for suburbs like Sugar Land, Cypress, Spring and League City, built with real local detail rather than swapped town names.
B2B and industrial firms: equipment, services and capability pages that procurement teams and engineers search for, plus content that makes you the obvious name for a niche.
Real estate and property: neighborhood guides and listing pages that rank in a city where buyers search by area.

p: A large share of Houstonians speak Spanish at home, and many search in it. For clinics, law firms, insurance agencies and home services, Spanish pages and a Spanish Google Business Profile description can reach people your competitors ignore. We write them properly, set up the language tags so Google serves the right version, and track Spanish keywords separately in your reports. It is one of the clearest gaps we find when we audit SEO. Houston competitors rarely do it well.

Right now, 10 of the businesses we work with sit in Google's top five for their main searches and show up in ChatGPT's answers. We got there with patient, specific work: technical clean-ups, honest content and consistent facts across the web, not shortcuts that a Google update can undo.

list: Talk: we learn your services, margins and the leads you actually want, not just the keywords you think you need.
Plan: an audit of your site, local listings and AI answers, followed by a 90-day plan with dates in writing.
Build: fixes, content and listings, shipped every month.
Grow: monthly reporting, AI answer rechecks and new content as rankings move.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take to work in Houston?
faqs.a: Technical fixes and Google Business Profile improvements can show results within weeks. Competitive searches, such as personal injury or dental in central Houston, usually take six to twelve months of steady work. We set expectations by keyword at the start and report progress monthly, so you can see what is moving and what is not.

faqs.q: Can you get us into ChatGPT and Google AI Overview answers?
faqs.a: We can make it much more likely, but nobody controls those answers. We make sure your business is described clearly and consistently on your site and across the web, write pages AI tools can quote, and check monthly how ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Google AI Overviews describe you. Then we fix what they get wrong.

faqs.q: Do you work with Houston law firms?
faqs.a: Yes. Monthly SEO and content for US personal injury firms is core work for us. Every legal claim, statute and deadline is checked before publishing, and pages respect Texas rules on lawyer advertising. We cover practice areas common in Houston, including truck, refinery and maritime injuries.

faqs.q: Do you meet Houston clients in person?
faqs.a: Our work is delivered remotely from London, with calls during your morning. SEO rarely needs a site visit, but if a photo shoot for your Google Business Profile or a planning session with your team would help, we arrange it when the project needs it. We have no Houston office.

faqs.q: We have several offices around Houston. How do you handle that?
faqs.a: Each office gets its own Google Business Profile, its own location page with real local detail, and its own reviews and citations. We track rankings from each area separately, because a result in Sugar Land tells you little about The Woodlands. Reporting shows each location side by side.
